main_body: A flat grass ground patch (4x3 tiles) with a repeating tuft pattern; terrain, not a standing object
top_band: none (flat ground texture; the column scan only shows repeating grass tone runs of mid green and dark tufts, not a top surface)
evidence: Terrain tile patch of grass, viewed as a flat ground surface. It is not a standing object, so the top/front contract does not apply. There is no standing volume, no side face and no elevation drawing. The repeating runs in the scan are grass tufts on a tiling pattern, not structural bands. Kind 'terrain' matches.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours and a median of 4 per tile, against 80 colours and a median of 26 per tile for the grass reference. 72% of its pixels sit in 5x5 flat-fill blocks, against 0% for the references. It is one mid-green base with sparse tufts of 2-3 pixels, repeated identically on a regular grid. The result is visibly mechanical, with no grain, no speckle and no clumps in several greens. Beside the Beodeul grass it looks thinner and flatter. It has no outline, which is fine for ground, and its tufts are tinted rather than neutral, but the shading depth and density are far below the bar.
